precepts.text: When you come to serve the Lord your iniquity is purged, and then you say, here am I, send me.
precepts.point: If the decayed state of your people does not move you to speak, the Lord is not using you.

note.label: TRUE UNITY AMONGST THE ISRAELITES

precepts.text: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Here am I; send me. That is the mindset of a leader, the same as David asking where Goliath was while everyone else cried about the situation.
precepts.point: The first mark of a leader's mindset: he believes he can get the job done. When an issue arises you do not run; you raise your hand, volunteer, and find the solution.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

precepts.text: Make the heart of this people fat and shut their eyes, lest they see and convert and be healed.
precepts.point: Leaders of other camps do not show up at IUIC schools unannounced and then complain on video about not being let in. There are channels; call first. The camps do not fellowship because of doctrine, and one GMS member sat in a school for months living a double life.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
The mist of darkness is reserved for those who speak evil of dignities and hate their brothers. Isaiah shows where that darkness comes from: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes”. Shut their eyes: darkness.

Why? “lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” Convert means repent. Lest they repent. The Lord shuts the eyes of the builders, the rulers, so they cannot see.

That is why Peter calls them “wells without water”, with no understanding. When you badmouth Peter, Paul, John the Baptist or any of the apostles and prophets, the Lord puts the spirit of darkness on you until you become a borderline, if not full-blown, Christianity teacher. Your ears are made heavy and your eyes are shut, and you cannot understand even the basic verses. Be mindful how you deal with brothers; brothers who murmur and speak evil bug out and go back into the world.

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed but understand not; the Lord makes their heart fat and shuts their eyes lest they see and convert.
precepts.point: The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the Lord has made both. When you battle with someone who does not understand, it is not their time; the Lord dulls the ears and closes the spiritual eyes so they cannot see or understand.

note.label: Proverbs 20: Integrity, Just Weights, and Waiting on the Lord

precepts.why:
“The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.” Hearing and seeing come from the Lord, and so does the lack of them.

Isaiah was sent with that very message: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” The Lord makes their heart fat and shuts their eyes, lest they see and convert. They have ears and eyes, but no understanding comes through them, because the Lord has closed them.

So when you battle with someone who does not understand, it is not their time. The Lord dulls the ears and closes the spiritual eyes so they cannot see or understand. He made the hearing ear and the seeing eye, and he decides when they open.

precepts.text: Christ spoke in parables so that seeing they see not and hearing they hear not, fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah.
precepts.point: Christ spoke in parables because it is not meant for everybody to get the understanding of the bible. Captain OC's class, The Purpose of Christ Told by the Israelites, opens this in detail.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

precepts.why:
“Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.” Christ carried this out with parables: “Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive”.

Christ spoke in parables so that seeing they see not and hearing they hear not, and in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled. It is not meant for everybody to get the understanding of the bible. Captain OC’s class, The Purpose of Christ Told by the Israelites, opens this in detail.

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed but understand not; their eyes are shut lest they convert and be healed.
precepts.point: The eyes of them that see shall not be dim and the ears of them that hear shall hearken; you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. The heart of the rash shall understand knowledge and the stammering tongue shall speak plainly.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.” That is the undoing of what Isaiah was sent to say at the first: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

Their eyes were shut and their ears made heavy lest they convert and be healed. Isaiah 32 is when that is lifted: you will begin to see spiritually and hear with understanding. “The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.”

precepts.text: Hear ye indeed, but understand not; make the heart of this people fat, lest they convert and be healed.
precepts.point: They saw the works and did not perceive. The heart was made fat and the ears heavy so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive”. Here is that prophecy as it was given to Isaiah: “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

They saw the works and did not perceive. Isaiah was told to make the heart of this people fat, make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, lest they convert and be healed. It was done to them on purpose, so that they would not be converted, because judgment had to come. Matthew says the same: their heart is waxed gross, their ears are dull of hearing, their eyes they have closed, “lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.” That is why he spoke to them in parables, and why the ones who heard him and saw his works did not understand.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why: “In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” Isaiah saw a vision of the Lord sitting on his throne in heaven. Isaiah is not in heaven with God; he is seeing a vision, seeing himself in the spiritual realm, in that counsel where the world was prepared for them that now live.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.” Isaiah sees himself in the heavens saying, send me, I’ll go.

We just read in 2 Esdras that the Lord said he’s going to send Isaiah back, and we just read another prophecy in 2 Esdras that before we came to this earth the Lord had already given us our assignment. So Isaiah stood up and said, I’ll go down there, send me. He said that in the heavens. You think Isaiah got time to be down here wasting his time like he ain’t got no purpose? You may be Isaiah, because the Bible did confirm that he’s here in the last days teaching, or going to be teaching. You ain’t got no time to play.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why: “And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” He gave him an assignment, what he wanted him to do. That is the assignment given before the spirit ever came down into the flesh.

note.label: The Getaway 3

precepts.why: These Pharisees were doctors of the law reading the prophecy of themselves, but they had that veil over their face. Some of our brothers today too: some of the Yaya reject Christ, the Old Testament Israelites, and even brothers who say yahawashi but don’t believe yahawashi brought in the New Covenant. “Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not”: the scribes saw Christ in the flesh and perceived not, even with the miracles. “Make the heart of this people fat”: some people the Most High just don’t want to wake up to this understanding. You might wake up to being an Israelite and to some high holy days, but the full understanding of Christ he’s blocking from you. Some of you are going to die in your sin rejecting Christ, and there ain’t going to be no mediator for you.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
“In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” The Lord here is Christ, the Word of God read in Wisdom of Solomon that leaped off his royal throne and came down as a man of war. This is his throne.

“Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.” The Lord of hosts here is Christ. Then Isaiah said, “Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.”

That is when John says Isaiah saw his glory and spoke of him. The King, the Lord of hosts, is the Word of God, Christ on his throne. And the Father has a throne too.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept that Isaiah would return. “Fear not, thou mother of the children: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord”: the mother is Jerusalem. “For thy help will I send my servants Esau and Jeremy.” Write that down in your Bible: on the computer it’ll say Esau, but that’s wrong. It’s Isaiah.

Ezra was during the Persian captivity. Isaiah had been dead already. God says here, I’m going to send Isaiah and I’m going to send Jeremiah, come back. They don’t know what you’re talking about. What Bible are they reading? Their spiritual eyes must be closed.

“After whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for thee twelve trees laden with divers fruits”: the twelve trees go back to the twelve apostles, which go with the twelve tribes. So Isaiah and Jeremiah would help them.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Jump back to the chapter before. “I take to witness the grace of the people to come, whose little ones rejoice in gladness”: whose little ones means your children. “And though they have not seen me with bodily eyes”: we’ve not seen the Lord with bodily eyes, “yet in spirit they believe the thing that I say”: in the spirit we believe everything this Bible says.

“And now, brother, behold what glory”, and see the people that come from the east, “Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham”: God said, I’m going to send Abraham back. Isaac, I’m going to send Isaac back. Jacob, I’ma send Jacob back. Oseas, that’s Hosea: I’m going to send the prophet Hosea back. Amos, Micheas, the prophet Micah, Joel, Abdias, that’s Obadiah, Jonas, the prophet Jonah, Nahum, Abacuc, the prophet Habakkuk, Sophonias, the prophet Zephaniah, Aggeus, the prophet Haggai, Zachary, the prophet Zechariah, “and Malachy, which is called also an angel of the Lord.”

So the Lord is sending these prophets back in these last days. That’s why they can’t stop this. We don’t know who’s who, but we know those prophets are back. They grew up in a grimy state; now they’re getting their minds right, and they’re going to come to the fulfillment of their spirit. You’ve got to believe that.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Revelation ties into the same thing. “And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Guess who’s part of that 144 thousand: Isaiah, Jeremiah, all them names we just read. They’re part of the 144 thousand. They’re coming back.

Christianity is trying to stop this, Islam is trying to stop this. You can’t stop this great awakening.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Watch what he says to the prophet John. This is scripture, Bible, proof that the prophets would be back in these last days. “And I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up”: the little book is the Bible. He studied it. “And it was in my mouth sweet as honey”: the Kingdom, that’s the sweetest honey. “And as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter.” You know why it was bitter? Because he saw a lot of death. He saw a lot of brothers and sisters falling off, going back into the world again, and the persecution. That’s the bitterness.

“And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” John died on the island of Patmos. So what you gonna do with that? What in the world does a Christian preacher have to say about this verse? They can’t even read it. There’s no interpretation but what it says; you don’t even have to interpret that.

That’s why it matters when the scriptures talk about loving your neighbor as yourself, and ask how you can say you love God, who you never see, but hate your brother. You might be hating on Father Abraham, Isaac or Jacob. You don’t know who you’re hating on.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why: Here’s that great awakening of them prophets of the 144 thousand. Like it was said during Men’s Conference, the 144 thousand are all apostles, every last one of them. “And after three days and an half”: after 350 years, “the Spirit of life from God entered into them”. The spirit of life is the Holy Spirit. “And they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” This is what y’all see right now, and it’s nothing to what it’s going to turn into, from state to state, country to country. Mark those words. That’s that fear: they want to shut this down, but it ain’t going to stop nothing.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
“Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath”. The breath is the Holy Spirit, the same as the spirit of life from God we just read about in Revelation 11; it’s talking about the same thing. “And breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them”: the Holy Spirit came into them, “and they lived”: their spirit lived, “and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” This is the word of God. These are the prophecies that we are living.

Look at the pictures of the brothers. If those men were committing crimes, doing something crazy, every camera would be there. Because of this, they act like they’re not seeing it, and they are struck with terrible fear: who the hell is organizing this? They know it’s the Most High. Like they write in them books: we know this is the Lord dealing with this, but we’re going to tell you it ain’t the Lord, you’re a bunch of fakers. Only the Lord can do something like this. All our lives they told us we were nobody, and now we find ourselves in the greatest movement on planet Earth.

But we should never be satisfied as long as we know our brothers on the other side of the world are being whooped and sold as slaves. We’ve got to go fish them.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Didn’t Christ say the same thing? This is Christ speaking: “And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand”: you Israelites, you don’t understand. “And seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people’s heart is waxed gross”: that’s what it means to make their heart fat, waxed gross. “And their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.”

The Lord is letting us know there’s a remnant allotted not to wake up. Some of your mothers, some of your fathers, some of your children will not wake up to this truth. They will fight you; they will come against you.

But you men and women, Christ said, “blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.”

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Christ said the same thing Isaiah said. Remember what we just read: until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, the houses without man, the land utterly desolate, and the Lord have removed men far away, and a great forsaking in the midst of the land. Watch what Christ says: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites that remain would fall by the edge of the sword, Rome’s sword, “and shall be led away captive into all nations”.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: so who’s going to live in Jerusalem? “Until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: until the time of the Gentile rulership be fulfilled. So Christ is saying the same thing that Isaiah said.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
We always read this. “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land”: see that word, land. Land, meaning this is about America, the land only, America. “Saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”: two parts of the Israelites here shall be cut off and die. “But the third shall be left therein”, meaning the third is going to repent.

The tenth of Isaiah 6:13 is more than this one third in America: it is Israel worldwide.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why: The precept for the holy seed. “For they have taken of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands.” We sinned, and it still refers to us as the holy seed. We are the holy seed. But as we read on, the holy seed begins with Christ.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why:
Here’s an analogy that Job gives about the tree, so you can get the visual. “For there is hope of a tree”: remember, we’re talking about the teil tree and the oak tree, “if it be cut down, that it will sprout again”. Although you cut it down, Job says it’s going to sprout again, “and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.”

God gave the same analogy to Isaiah for us. Although we got destroyed as a nation, as a people, as a race, the substance is still in them; the Holy Spirit is still going to reactivate them, reawaken them.

“Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground; Yet through the scent of water”: the scent of water is God’s word, “it will bud”: you’ll start to grow again. That’s what you’re seeing right now, “and bring forth boughs like a plant.”

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why: “The remnant shall return, even the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God.” See that: the remnant shall return. “For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return”: that’s that tenth we were just reading about. “The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.”

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

precepts.why: It’s the same analogy: you’ve got a stump. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse”: a plant is going to grow out of the stump of Jesse, “and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”. This is talking about Christ. That’s why he’s the first of the holy seed: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord”. Without Christ we would not be here; it had to start with him.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why: This shows how the Israelites were removed far away. “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”: Christ is going to bring back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, meaning bring us back into our own land.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why:
“The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” This is Tyre and Zidon, and Palestine. They enslaved us and sold us to the white man to remove us far from our borders. That’s how we are here in America and throughout the Caribbean islands: the Arabs and the Africans sold us to the white man.

“Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head”: what you did to them is going to be returned on your own head. That’s future prophecy.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why:
“By the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him”: before Christ returns, we will be gathered together unto him. “That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” Don’t let nobody tell you the day of Christ is at hand. Paul said this because there were dudes back then teaching that the resurrection had already taken place.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first”. That’s what we read in Isaiah 6: that falling away first is the great forsaking. We had to be led away in slavery into all nations, and the remembrance of us had to cease from among men. Back then, when we were in the land and Christ was there, we knew who we were. The apostles knew: I’m Judah. But prophecy had to be fulfilled, where nobody would look at us and say these are the children of Israel.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

precepts.why:
In slavery they gave us their ways so we would lose who we are, and that’s the same mindset still. Scattered among the nations, the nations are not going to teach you that you are the children of Israel or that you have to repent as an Israelite; they hide your identity from you. That’s why God keeps sending the prophets to bring you back out of all this captivity.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”. Remember the remembrance of us was to cease from among men. Who is saying we are not God’s people? The people today, the so-called white man: you’re not the Israelites.

“There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” How is it being said? That’s us teaching in the streets: yes, we are the sons of the living God, what the hell you talking about. In the place is America, it’s Europe, all these lands where they say you are African-Americans, you are Puerto Ricans, all these names they give us. We are going to rise up and say that we are the sons of the living God.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

precepts.why:
Back to John to weigh it again: “That the saying of” Isaiah “the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?” “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” The I that should heal them is the Lord, Christ. That’s what Isaiah saw.

“These things said” Isaiah “when he saw his glory, and spake of him”: he spoke of Christ. That is who Isaiah was speaking about in Isaiah 6. He saw the Lord of hosts, he saw the King, and that was Christ: he saw him in his eternal form in the heavens. Remember Corinthians 15: the last Adam is the Lord from heaven.

When the spirit opened this up, it was plain: the Lord we read about right through the scripture is Christ on the throne. It is not until the end that we see the Father, in Daniel 7. That’s Christ’s Father.

points: In the year that King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Most High sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple. The train is his cape, so long that it flowed out behind him and filled the whole temple.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: Above the throne stood the seraphims, each one having six wings. With two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he did fly; twain means two.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: One cried to another, "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory." The posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: Isaiah says, "Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts."
When men see the Most High or the day of the Most High, terror comes upon them and they cry, "Woe is me." Another prophet said he hoped he would not be living when that time came.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: Then flew one of the seraphims with a live coal in his hand, taken with the tongs from off the altar, and laid it upon Isaiah's mouth, saying his iniquity is taken away and his sin purged.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: Isaiah heard the voice of the Most High saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?" and answered, "Here am I; send me."

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: He was sent to tell this people, "Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not."

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: The Most High says to make the heart of this people fat, their ears heavy, and shut their eyes, lest they see, hear, understand with their heart, convert, and be healed.
Christ spoke in parables because it is not meant for everybody to get the understanding of the bible. Captain OC's class, The Purpose of Christ Told by the Israelites, opens this in detail.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: Isaiah asks, "Lord, how long?" and is answered, "Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate."

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: The Most High will remove men far away, and there will be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: Yet a tenth shall return and be eaten, as a teil tree and as an oak whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves; the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

note.label: Isaiah 6: The Prophet's Vision and Commission

points: “In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” His train was the garment.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “Above it stood the seraphims”: the seraphims are angels, high ranking top angels. Their job was to cover the throne. Like the Ark of the Covenant: you had images of angels over the mercy seat, and that was represented from the kingdom of heaven, where the Lord was sitting on the throne and you had the seraphims on either side.
“Each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.” Twain means two.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: This is Isaiah speaking before the Lord God: “I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips”, talking about the Israelites, a people of unclean lips. “For mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts”: this King, the Lord of hosts, is Christ. That’s who it’s talking about.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “Having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.” The tongs are like when you cook and you pick it up with that, a fork or whatever. The angel came and took out a coal.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “And he laid it upon my mouth”: the angel took the coal and laid it on Isaiah’s mouth, “and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.” Isaiah’s sin was being purged from him.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” The Lord is asking, who can I send back to the earth for us, to teach the world of the Most High. “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” Remember we’re in Isaiah chapter six: this is a prophecy that Isaiah would return. Isaiah said, send me, Lord.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “And he said, Go”: the Lord said to Isaiah, go, “and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” He’s talking about the Israelites. This people: we hear the scriptures but we don’t understand; we see what the Bible is saying but we don’t indeed perceive it.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes”: shut their spiritual eyes, “lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

Look at the church pictures: cobwebs all back there, and blind people in the church. They can’t see it with spiritual eyes, they can’t hear with their spiritual ears, they can’t understand the Bible. Our job is to go tell them, like Christ.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “Then said I, Lord, how long?” How long will this be, Lord? “And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant”: until Jerusalem, Israel, is wasted, with no Israelites remaining there; “and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate.” He’s talking about 70 A.D. All the Israelites either ran out, got caught in slavery, or were murdered.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “And the Lord have removed men far away”: the Lord removed the Israelite men far away, “and there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.”

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “But yet in it shall be a tenth.” Pay close attention to that. This tenth here is more than the one third in America. This tenth is talking about Israel worldwide. Remember, we were scattered; we were removed into all places. God said in Israel there’s going to be a tenth that’s going to come back. So that’s not just America: that’s Africa, that’s Europe, that’s the Caribbean islands, that’s over in the Iran areas. “It” is Israel, “and it shall return”: that tenth shall return to the one true God, “and shall be eaten”.

Look at the imagery: “as a teil tree, and as an oak”. It’s giving you the image of a tree cut down, two trees cut down. Why two trees? Because we’re split into two kingdoms. Can that tree live again? Yeah, because all you need is that one little sprout to come up, and that tree will live again. That’s what he’s saying here.

“Whose substance is in them”: that substance is God’s spirit, the reawakening of God’s spirit that’s in us, “when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.” The holy seed begins with Christ; that’s the only way that substance can come back.

note.label: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

points: “Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant”: the cities of Israel have got to be destroyed without inhabitants, none of us living in that land anymore. That’s what you see going on. We not in that land no more; you might have one or two of our brothers over there, but they’re subjugated under Esau. “And the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate”.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: “And the Lord have removed men far away”: the men he’s removing far away are the 12 tribes of Israel, far away into captivity. That goes with ‘I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men.’

“And there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land”: we forsook our identity, we left our culture. We fled the land of Israel from persecution and lived in all these different countries, scattered toward the four corners of the earth in slavery. That’s the great forsaking.

Read it again after Joel 3: we were removed far away by the Africans and the Arabs selling us to the Grecians. That’s what Isaiah is talking about, and the great forsaking in the midst of the land is because of slavery.

note.label: Escape New Years | Armageddon: Chain Of Events

points: An ambassador is an accredited diplomat sent by a country as its official representative to a foreign country. That is what the brothers are: ambassadors, sent ones.

God asks, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And Isaiah answers, “Then said I, Here am I”. The prophet volunteered: Lord, send me. That is the same spirit as each and every one in the room. This is for the brothers, because they are the ambassadors, the bold witnesses for the kingdom.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

points: This is Christ’s glory and what Isaiah saw. “In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord”: the Lord here is the same Lord in Corinthians, the second Adam, the Lord from heaven, the Lord come down from heaven. Isaiah saw Christ. He saw the word of God, the Lord the God of Israel, the one that created the heavens and the earth and that created Israel, “sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” This is the Lord Isaiah saw.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “Each one had six wings”: these are the angels that are around Christ, “with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.”

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.” Who is the Lord of hosts? Christ.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips”. This is how Isaiah felt when he saw the Lord: he saw Christ in his glory, sitting on his throne in heaven, because that’s where he is. He dwelt “in the midst of a people of unclean lips”, and his eyes saw “the King, the Lord of hosts”: he saw our King, Christ, and he knew who he was. He knew the Lord of hosts.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: One flew to him with a live coal “taken with the tongs from off the altar: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.” Your sins are taken away. The Lord can take away your sins just like that. Brothers, understand that once you are one of the elect, and you are trying hard and you are sincere in this walk, the Lord is going to show you mercy.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go for us? That is the same as let us create man in our image: that is the powers in the heaven. Guess what: Christ’s Father is not there. It is Christ and the angels. “Then said I, Here am I; send me.”

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: What does God tell Isaiah to do? “Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” You hear it and you don’t understand; you see, but you don’t perceive. “Make the heart of this people fat”, and “shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes”, “and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed”: healed by the Lord.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway
